Playbook.name: AD — SPN Added by Non-Computer Principal (Kerberoast Setup) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A servicePrincipalName was added (5136) by a non-computer, non-SYSTEM principal - attackers set an SPN on a user account they control so it becomes Kerberoastable. Triage question: legitimate service registration by an app admin, or an attacker priming a target for roasting?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Adding an SPN to a user account makes its (often weak) password crackable via a service ticket - a self-service route to a stronger credential.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: SPN write by user
Signal.Details: 5136 AttributeLDAPDisplayName servicePrincipalName, subject not a machine account or SYSTEM.

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: Object the SPN was added to (ObjectDN).

InitialAssessment.Rule: App/service registration by an app-admin onto a service account is routine; a user setting an SPN on itself or a peer user account is the roast-setup shape.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the SPN registration is legitimate service onboarding or Kerberoast preparation.

Step.name: Detail the SPN change and target object type
Step.Purpose: Target being a normal USER account (not a service/computer) is the key roast-setup indicator.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("5136","5137") AND winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "servicePrincipalName" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.ObjectDN, winlog.event_data.AttributeValue, event.code | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: ObjectDN in a service/OU=Service Accounts container = onboarding. ObjectDN being a regular user (especially the actor themselves) = roast setup.

Step.name: Was the SPN immediately roasted (RC4 4769)
Step.Purpose: An SPN set and then a service ticket requested for it within minutes is the roast chain executing.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4769" AND winlog.event_data.ServiceName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS req = COUNT(*), enc = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, src | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A 4769 (especially RC4 0x17) for the just-SPN'd account confirms the roast chain. Empty result does not clear it - roasting may follow later.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the SPN added to a normal user account (or self) by a non-admin, and/or INV-02 shows an immediate RC4 ticket request.
Node.Result: True Positive (Kerberoast Setup - escalate, reset target)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows registration onto a service account within a service-accounts container by an application/IAM admin.
Non-standard actor but target is plausibly a service account and no roast followed - provenance unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SPN-CHANGE, INV-02-SPN-ROAST to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Legitimate service onboarding registering an SPN on a service account.

Indicators.Item: Target is a service account in the expected container.

SOCAction.Item: Verify onboarding record; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Attacker set an SPN on a controlled account to make it Kerberoastable.

Indicators.Item: SPN added to a regular user or the actor's own account.
Immediate RC4 service-ticket request for it.
Actor is not a service admin.

SOCAction.Item: Remove the SPN; reset the target account with a strong password.
Investigate the actor; open IR if roasted.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automation registering SPNs too broadly due to misconfiguration.

Indicators.Item: Provisioning account adding SPNs per a broken template.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the automation; remove stray SPNs.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Remove the SPN if illegitimate; reset the target account.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Check for roasting of the target and other accounts by the same actor.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict who can write servicePrincipalName; monitor SPN additions.

QualityChecks.Check: Rule excludes machine accounts and SYSTEM; AttributeValue holds the SPN string.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Service onboarding confirmed; target is a proper service account.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: SPN removed, target reset, actor investigated.
